title: promote-latest.mjs resume path: a launcher that npm still reads absent or integrity-null can roll back a correct release
description: From the LCLI-689 confirmatory review of d4d9dfa6 (NEW FINDINGS), alongside LCLI-747. (b) MOST IMPORTANT: on a resume, if npm still reads the launcher as absent while its dist-tags already show X, the resume plans a publish; the publish fails because the version exists, and promote() then restores every tag, rolling back a correct release. Only the remedy's re-read-first ordering guards it. (a) the resume's step 8 (about promote-latest.mjs:1796) treats a null dist.integrity as a mismatch ("needs a new version, not a rerun") where publishFinalLauncher (:1072) treats the same state as lag; make them agree. Also: (c) the tags exit-1 remedy (:1947) should also name the npm view <launcher>@X dist.integrity re-read; (d) the integrity wait (verifyFinalLauncher) and the --rollback restore wait are unannounced, so the silent worst case is about twice the printed bound; (e) the rollback-window test converges on read 1 and does not pin the 121-read bound; (f) the CHANGELOG line "the exit-1 messages say nothing was rolled back" is untrue of the integrity-MISMATCH exit, which prescribes --rollback. Not built.
